scope: Theorem 5.1 (Exact step and its comparison estimates) of the manuscript “Sharp mass bounds for the two-dimensional O(4) model” (preprints/Sharp-mass-bounds-for-the-two-dimensional-O4-model-September-23-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 215 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 e87f407df77777ca), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 41. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: The constants can be chosen in the order described below so that integration by (5.2), from an input with b ∈ [Hj/2, 2Hj], gives an exact representation (5.10) on layer j − 1, with free history h + 1, all the renewed norm bounds, and b′ = b + αh(P) + κh(P) b + ∆, |αh| + |κh| ≤ CL, |∆| ≤ CLH−1.05 j . (5.11) The canonical map and αh, κh depend only on the input canonical vector P and the free history. They do not depend on the precise coupling, the cutoffs, the errors, the covering gas, or the period. The output is iterable if its coupling belongs to the next admitted band; this additional fact is proved for the trajectories used below. For two inputs on common label lists and the same reference layer, let λ = b2 − b1. Let u be a fixed positively weighted sum of the seven coefficient discrepancies, the error discrepancy δ−1 j ∥f2 − f1∥k−1,j,A, and the gas discrepancy w−1 j ∥k2 − k1∥j,A. The weights are independent of j and the periods. The outputs have common compatible lists and satisfy u′ ≤ qu + CLHC j ϵh + CLH−b∗ j |λ|, (5.12) |λ′ − λ| ≤ CLu + CLHC j ϵh + CLH−b∗ j |λ|, (5.13) where L−1 < q < 1, b∗ > 0, and ϵh = L− min(h1,h2) for unequal free histories (zero for equal histories). These estimates include bulk and all admitted periods.
